texas-football.summary: Texas comes out of its bye for Oklahoma with Sarkisian reporting better overall health, but no individual clearance yet. First-down efficiency and a disciplined pass rush are the priorities in Dallas.

items.headline: Sarkisian reports better health; individual statuses remain pending
items.tldr: Monday’s assessment was encouraging, but it did not clear individual players. Check the availability report before assuming the full rotation is back.

items.headline: Texas’s six three-and-outs at Tennessee began with poor first downs
items.tldr: Burnt Orange Nation’s review found four of those six opening plays lost at least four yards. Watch whether Texas can avoid penalties and negative plays before the defense knows a pass is coming.

items.headline: Simmons set a Texas record with 5.5 sacks at Tennessee
items.tldr: The record describes the September 26 game, not a projection for Dallas. Watch whether the edge pressure can hurry Oklahoma’s quarterback while keeping an escape lane covered.

items.headline: Oklahoma gave up 17 points off four turnovers at Georgia
items.tldr: The Sooners’ last game shows why possession swings matter. Texas should try to force difficult decisions, then give its offense a useful field position.

items.headline: Texas–Florida is set for 11 a.m. CT on October 17
items.tldr: The network remains ABC or ESPN, with the final choice due after October 10. Plan for the early start next week while this week’s focus stays on Oklahoma.

lead.headline: Win first down.
lead.body: Avoid the early loss that turns a possession into an obvious passing situation. On defense, close the pocket without letting the quarterback escape through the middle.

matchup.question: What should Texas emphasize against Oklahoma?
matchup.answer: Use the available short throw or running lane to stay ahead of the chains. Make the quarterback move without abandoning containment, and be ready to capitalize on a turnover.

utah-state-football.summary: Utah State hosts Washington State on Friday with its starting quarterback still unannounced. Jacobs’ rushing and Wood’s receiving offer ways to build drives; the defense must avoid another quick answer after a score.

items.headline: Mendenhall has not named Friday’s starting quarterback
items.tldr: Monday’s update left the choice unresolved after both quarterbacks played at Boise State. Follow the final decision and watch whether the offense can build a rhythm with its practice preparation.

items.headline: Local analysis calls for steadier involvement from Eli Wood
items.tldr: Cache Valley Daily traced how Wood’s targets disappeared between productive drives at Boise State. Watch whether the passing game keeps finding him when the first series is over.

items.headline: Jacobs rushed for 139 yards at Boise State
items.tldr: His first 100-yard rushing game gives the offense something to build on. Watch the blocks that create space and whether Utah State can turn a long gain into a finished drive.

items.headline: Washington State scored only on two field goals against Fresno State
items.tldr: The Cougars lost 26-6 and went scoreless after halftime. Utah State should make them sustain a drive, with sound coverage and tackles instead of a quick explosive play.

items.headline: Friday’s home game starts at 7 p.m. MT on The CW
items.tldr: Maverik Stadium gates open at 5:30 p.m., and fans are asked to wear blue. Set the earlier arrival or broadcast reminder now: this is a Friday game.

lead.headline: Keep the next drive alive.
lead.body: Find the available throw, give the runner room and make the next tackle. After scoring, the defense needs to hold its coverage long enough to earn another possession.

matchup.question: What should Utah State emphasize on Friday?
matchup.answer: Keep the productive receivers involved and take the available running lane. On defense, communicate through changes in formation and finish the tackle before a short gain becomes a long one.

ohio-state-football.summary: Ohio State returns home for Maryland after Jeremiah Smith’s 206-yard receiving game at Iowa. Day wants better special teams and says Wilder and Bey still have to earn opportunities in practice.

items.headline: Day says Ohio State needs better special-teams production
items.tldr: Tuesday’s criticism covered kicking, punting and both return units. Watch the operation and coverage on each kick, rather than judging the unit by one long field goal.

items.headline: Day says Wilder and Bey must earn their opportunities
items.tldr: Neither played against Iowa. Day hopes to use them against Maryland if practice goes well; that is a conditional plan, not a promised role.

items.headline: Smith caught 11 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns at Iowa
items.tldr: Watch how Ohio State creates room for its receivers against Maryland. The next useful gain can come from the open outlet as well as the difficult catch downfield.

items.headline: Maryland’s Durr had seven catches for 149 yards at Nebraska
items.tldr: The opponent preview identifies a receiver who can keep possessions moving. Watch Ohio State’s first tackle after the catch, especially on throws underneath the coverage.

items.headline: Maryland visits Saturday at 4:15 p.m. ET on Big Ten Network
items.tldr: Set the afternoon viewing plan for Homecoming. On the field, watch Ohio State’s protection against Maryland’s pass rush before looking for the downfield throw.

lead.headline: Make every possession count.
lead.body: Keep the passing game moving, finish tackles on Maryland’s underneath throws and avoid surrendering field position on special teams.

matchup.thesis: Pair passing production with clean execution
matchup.question: What should Ohio State improve against Maryland?
matchup.answer: Find the available receiver without forcing the ball, rally to short completions and handle the kick cleanly. Watch whether the younger players earn work during the game.

lsu-football.summary: LSU heads to Kentucky after its 63-14 win over McNeese. Green is out of his brace but has no confirmed return, while Kentucky’s latest coaching focus is third-down execution on both sides of the ball.

items.headline: Kiffin says Green is out of his brace and getting closer
items.tldr: Monday’s recovery update did not confirm a return date or clearance for Kentucky. Check the availability report, then watch how the available tight ends are used.

items.headline: LSU scored six rushing touchdowns against McNeese
items.tldr: The 63-14 win featured 731 yards of total offense. Watch whether the blocking and ball security can carry into an SEC road game, where each finished possession matters.

items.headline: Stein wants better third-down execution on both sides
items.tldr: Kentucky’s coach pointed Tuesday to route detail on offense and quarterback scrambles allowed on defense. Watch LSU’s protection and whether its own rush keeps the quarterback contained.

items.headline: Kentucky’s tight ends finished its overtime win at South Carolina
items.tldr: Minchey found Boyer for the touchdown, then Rodriguez for the winning two-point conversion. Watch LSU’s coverage communicate near the goal line, including when a tight end releases late.

items.headline: LSU’s October 17 homecoming game is set for 11 a.m. CT
items.tldr: Mississippi State visits next week on ABC or ESPN. The final network will be selected after October 10; the early kickoff is already confirmed.

lead.headline: Earn the road possessions.
lead.body: Keep the running game on schedule and the quarterback protected. On defense, finish the tackle before the quarterback turns a passing down into another first down.

matchup.question: What should LSU emphasize at Kentucky?
matchup.answer: Set up manageable third downs, use the available running lane and contain the quarterback when coverage holds. Be ready for the tight end when Kentucky gets close to the goal line.
